reasoning:
The retrieved Acme fragments show elements of a risk-assessment program that map to the Article 9(2)(a) requirement but do not fully mirror it. ACME-POL-AIGOV-002 section 5 (Pre-Deployment Risk Assessment) requires a pre-deployment assessment covering intended purpose/use cases, data sources/quality, known limitations, and fairness/bias considerations, which supports identification of some risks (particularly bias/fundamental-rights related risks) and ties assessment to intended purpose. The Model Risk Management Standard (ACME-POL-MRM-003 section 1) also establishes requirements to identify, assess and manage model risk. Roles and responsibilities (ACME-POL-AIGOV-002 section 6) show governance and independent review, which supports an organizational capability to perform risk analysis.

What is missing or unclear versus the regulatory text: (1) none of the fragments explicitly require identification and analysis of "known and reasonably foreseeable risks" phrased as such (the policy mentions "known limitations" but not "reasonably foreseeable" future risks); (2) the fragments do not explicitly require that risks to "health, safety or fundamental rights" be identified and analysed (fairness/bias is present, but health/safety and the full scope of fundamental rights are not named); (3) the policy appears focused on pre-deployment assessment and model-risk processes, so it is unclear whether ongoing identification/analysis during use (i.e., when the system is used in accordance with its intended purpose over time) is required; and (4) there is no explicit methodological or documentation requirement shown for how to perform the required "analysis" (depth, metrics, or required outputs/controls are not specified in the fragments).

Recommendation: treat these fragments as indicating potential impact (the bank already has relevant processes), but a human Compliance Analyst should verify gaps and determine whether the policy must be amended to explicitly cover "reasonably foreseeable" risks, explicitly name health/safety/fundamental rights, require lifecycle/operational assessment, and define required analysis outputs and documentation.

citations.internal: ACME-POL-AIGOV-002, 5. Risk Assessment Prior to Deployment

retrieved_fragments.excerpt:
Before any AI system is deployed to production, the owning business unit must
complete a Pre-Deployment Risk Assessment covering:

- Intended purpose and use cases
- Data sources and data quality
- Known limitations of the model or system
- Fairness and bias considerations
- Sign-off from the AIGC for high-impact systems

- **Chief AI Officer**: overall accountability for the AI governance framework
- **AI Governance Committee**: approval authority for high-impact systems
- **Business Unit Owner**: day-to-day operational accountability for each system
- **Model Risk Function**: independent review of model risk (see the separate
  Model Risk Management Standard)

retrieved_fragments.policy_title: Acme Bank Model Risk Management Standard

This Standard sets out the requirements for identifying, assessing, and managing
model risk across all quantitative models used by Acme Bank, including statistical,
machine learning, and AI-based models.
